title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pages ~575-577 of Grothendieck's numbering; archive p.546). The setting is the 'loop equation' (équation des lacets) analysis of how an element u acts on a profinite group 𝔊. Here u is an element of a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-like group or of Γ_Q, with multiplier μ = χ(u) in Ẑ^*. 𝔊 is a quotient of Γ̂_{1,1}, the profinite completion of the full (orientation-reversing) modular group of the once-punctured torus, Γ̂_{1,1} ≃ GL(2,Z)^. It is generated by ρ, σ, τ' with:
- ρ^6 = σ^4 = τ'^2 = 1;
- ρ^3 = σ^2 = −1 (central);
- τ' inverting both ρ and σ.

The oriented part 𝔊^+ = ⟨ρ,σ⟩ is the image of Γ̂^+_{1,1} ≃ SL(2,Z)^.

The action of u is described by a pair (α, β):
- u(ρ) = int(α)ρ, which conjugates ρ^μ back to ρ^{±1}; the sign is the conductor-3 character ε_3(μ).
- u(σ) = ε·int(β)σ, with ε = ε_2(μ) = (−1)^{(μ−1)/2}, the conductor-4 character.
- The loop/compatibility equation (68): αρ(α)^{-1} = ε βσ(β)^{-1} ℓ_1^ν, with ν = (μ−1)/2 mod 2, so (−1)^ν = ε.

The sign ε arises because in SL(2,Z), σ and σ^{-1} = −σ are not conjugate. They become conjugate in GL(2,Z) via τ', since τ'στ'^{-1} = σ^{-1}. So Grothendieck replaces β by β' = β twisted by τ'^ν. This absorbs the sign and gives the cleaner (69):
- u(ρ) = int(α)ρ;
- u(σ) = int(β')σ;
- αρ(α)^{-1} = β'σ(β')^{-1} ℓ_1^ν.

The sign information now sits in the orientation (determinant) characters (70): χ(α) = ε_3(μ), χ(β') = ε_2(μ). That is, α and β' are taken in the full GL-type group, not in SL.

He concludes that the GL(2)-quotient 𝔊' deserves the simple name 𝔊, with 𝔊^+ for the SL-part. He decides to redo the constructions 'à main levée' in these notations. He imposes the hypothesis τ ∉ 𝔊^+, equivalently (71) τ' ∉ 𝔊^+, i.e. orientation-reversal survives in the quotient. The next page starts §V 'Données préliminaires' with exactly this presentation of 𝔊.

The purpose is bookkeeping for the genus-1 (Γ_{1,1}) part of the Galois/GT action on profinite Teichmüller groups. Allowing orientation-reversing conjugators removes the quadratic-character signs from the loop equations.
errors: Order of multiplication: if int(β)σ means βσβ^{-1}, the sign is absorbed only with β' = β·τ'^ν (right multiplication). Then β'σβ'^{-1} = βσ^{ε}β^{-1} = ε·βσβ^{-1}, and β'σβ'^{-1}σ^{-1} = ε·βσβ^{-1}σ^{-1}, consistent with (69).

The previous page writes β' = τ'^ν β (left multiplication). That gives τ'(βσβ^{-1})τ'^{-1} = τ'(β)σ^{-1}τ'(β)^{-1}, which is not ε·βσβ^{-1} in general. So either the convention for int/action is reversed or there is a slip; it is harmless once fixed.
Minor: (70) is presented as where the sign 'reappears'. It is a restatement of the determinants of α and β', not a new constraint.

ideas.what: Presentation of GL(2,Z)^ (Γ̂_{1,1} with orientation reversal) by ρ (order 6), σ (order 4), τ' (order 2) with ρ^3=σ^2 central and τ' inverting ρ and σ; SL(2,Z)^ as the index-2 'oriented' subgroup.
ideas.modern_name: GL2(Z) ≅ D_6 *_{D_2} D_4-type amalgam; profinite completion of the extended mapping class group of the once-punctured torus
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses Γ_{1,1}, SL2(Z)^ and the Teichmüller tower in general terms

ideas.what: Galois/GT action on SL(2,Z)^ described by conjugators α, β satisfying a loop equation; orientation characters of conjugators given by conductor-3 and conductor-4 quadratic characters of the multiplier μ (ε_3(μ), ε_2(μ)).
ideas.modern_name: Action of GT^ / G_Q on the profinite genus-one modular group (genus-one GT relations)

ideas.what: Removing the sign ε by twisting the conjugator β by τ'^ν (passing from SL- to GL-conjugation), since σ and σ^{-1} are GL- but not SL-conjugate.
ideas.modern_name: Using the extended (orientation-reversing) modular group to normalize Galois cocycles

missed.claim: Grothendieck's explicit normalization: in the genus-one loop equation, taking conjugators in GL(2,Z)^ makes the equation sign-free, with det α = ε_3(μ) and det β' = ε_2(μ). This is a small but clean bookkeeping device. The published genus-one GT literature works mainly in SL2/±1 and does not phrase it this way, as far as I know.
missed.quote: et le signe ε = ε_2(μ) disparaît. Il apparaît dans les formules χ(α) = ε_3(μ), χ(β') = ε_2(μ)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It could slightly simplify the treatment of real structures / complex conjugation in the GT action on Γ_{1,1}, but it is not a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: Notational reorganization within Grothendieck's unpublished genus-one Galois-action computations. The sign-elimination via GL2 and the quadratic-character determinants are natural and easy, so there is no substantive new theorem on this page.
transcription_corrections: In (68) and (69), 'χλ(α)' / 'χλ(β')' should read 'int(α)' / 'int(β')' (inner automorphism), as on the previous page.
The marginal insertion reads approximately 'quotient de Γ̂_{1,1} ≃ GL(2,Z)^', not 'générateur de'. This matches the next page, where 𝔊 is defined as a quotient of GL(2,Z)^.
'Il me semble au moins un cours [?] pour pouvoir reprendre' is uncertain. The sense is 'it seems to me worthwhile/time to resume the constructions by hand with more adequate notations'.
The archive page number is 546; Grothendieck's own numbering would be 576, between 575 and 577.
